subject: Urgent: Skyline - sustained 5xx/429 spike, autoscale lag and retry amplification
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@skylineai.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@skylineai.com>, Skyline Ops <ops@skylineai.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: High 5xx/429 rates across inference endpoints - urgent

Marcus —

We started seeing a large spike in 5xx and 429 errors around 08:47 PST that’s persisted for ~90 minutes. Latency for short-chat endpoints jumped from p50=60ms to p50=420ms and p95s are >2s. Retries from our client side are amplifying the spike. We’ve attached the service logs and a Datadog snapshot.

Our product team is escalating since this affects core UX for customers on the Skyline platform. Can you confirm if this is a Dedicated pool capacity issue or an autoscale lag on Redwood’s side? If needed, we need an emergency fallback plan (model downgrade, rate-limiting, or host fallback).

Jordan
CTO, Skyline AI
[Attachment: svc-logs-20270214.zip (1.1MB)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@skylineai.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:25:37 -08:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 rates across inference endpoints - urgent

Jordan — thanks for the flag and the logs. I’m pulling the on-call and ops. Initial read: the traces show repeated 5xx returned by our dedicated pool colocated in us-west with a backlog and a long autoscale decision loop. The retry pattern from the Skyline client is contributing to queue buildup.

Immediate steps we’re recommending now (I’ll coordinate exec notification):
- Disable aggressive client retries (recommend exponential backoff + jitter) — Skyline to push a short patch if possible.
- Enable short-term failover to our hosted fallback pool (lower-cost model) while we stabilize Dedicated.
- Temp reduce Skyline concurrency quota to reduce amplification.
- Ops will push an emergency scale-up for the Dedicated pool and remove unhealthy nodes from rotation.

Neha is engaged to run repro and metrics correlation. Stephanie will lead the scale and fallback ops. Rachel will open an incident in our status system and prepare customer comms draft. I’ll loop in Sean for SLA/credits discussion if this meets the bar.

I’ll send a runbook with actions in the next 10–15m.

— Marcus
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@skylineai.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:34:02 -08:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 rates across inference endpoints - urgent

Following up with quick findings from the traces and metrics:
- 08:46–09:10 spike shows sustained GPU allocation exhaustion on pool us-west-dedicated-3 (queue depth rising >500).
- Autoscaler took ~6m to trigger a scale event due to conservative thresholds; then an additional 4m to warm VMs and load models.
- Evictions and KV cache misses on warmup drove a short phase of elevated 5xx as models load.
- Client retry cycles from Skyline (~3 retries, 100ms linear) created a retry storm centered on their 50k TPS window.

Immediate ops actions taken:
- Marked us-west-dedicated-3:draining and routed new traffic to other pools where capacity existed.
- Triggered manual scale + pre-warm for us-west-dedicated-4.
- Enabled hosted fallback route for Skyline’s account (read-only until stable).

Attaching the Datadog snapshot and logs: dd-dashboard-snapshot-20270214.png.

-Neha
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: dd-dashboard-snapshot-20270214.png (240KB)]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:50:11 -08:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 rates across inference endpoints - urgent

Ops update (action log):
- 09:02 manual drain initiated for node group us-west-dedicated-3; unhealthy nodes removed.
- 09:05 manual scale request issued to infra-controller with warm-image policy (expected ready ~09:16).
- 09:12 hosted-fallback route enabled for Skyline account; traffic shimmed at 20% initial load.
- 09:20 observed p95 latency drop from 2.2s to 1.1s on fallback; native pool still strained.
- 09:25 implemented temporary account-level concurrency cap (50 RPS) per API key to reduce retry amplification.

Next: run a short canary routing for 10m to validate KV cache warming; if stable, gradually shift more traffic. Rachel, please publish a holding statement; Marcus, can you confirm customer-facing ask re: concurrency cap?

-Stephanie
Director, Dedicated Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@skylineai.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@skylineai.com>, Skyline Ops <ops@skylineai.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 10:04:58 -08:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 rates across inference endpoints - urgent

Appreciate the rapid response. Two quick asks from our side: 1) we need a clear fallback and ETA that preserves correctness for our highest-value customers; 2) procurement is asking for any potential credit/financial remediation given the disruption (I’ve cc’d procurement).

If hosted fallback has different model variants, we need to confirm quality impact and whether embedding outputs are preserved. Also please share the proposed remediation in writing so I can brief the execs.

—Jordan

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@skylineai.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Skyline outage post-mortem & immediate remediation summary

Jordan / team — follow-up after today’s stabilization. Summary and next steps: 

Root cause: combination of (a) Dedicated pool us-west-dedicated-3 GPU exhaustion during a sudden traffic pattern change, (b) conservative autoscaler thresholds that delayed scale-out, and (c) client retry behavior creating a retry storm that amplified queueing.

What we did (timeline):
- Immediate: enabled hosted-fallback route (20% → 100% in 40m) and applied account-level concurrency cap.
- Ops: manual scale + pre-warm of dedicated nodes; unhealthy nodes removed and replaced.
- Infra: adjusted autoscaler thresholds for short-lived bursts; implemented pre-warm policy for critical accounts (applies to Skyline).
- Product: will ship a retry-protection guide + SDK change recommendation preventing linear 100ms rapid retries (ETA 1 week).

Customer impact: transient 5xx/429 spike for ~70 minutes affecting 3% of production requests; p95 latency degraded during that window.

Remediation & commitments: 
- Temporary credit: Redwood will propose a good-faith service credit — Sean, please pick up the dollar figure with finance and circle back to Jordan directly.
- Permanent fixes: autoscaler tuning, pre-warm for key Dedicated pools, improved warm-start diagnostics, and a customer SDK retry guard.
- Follow-up: post-mortem doc and runbook + short technical war room for Skyline (we’ll schedule today).

Attachments: proposed-fallback-runbook.pdf (contains steps for failover, mapping of model variants and expected quality deltas).

Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed-fallback-runbook.pdf (220KB)]
